clue.text: Unreliable : witness ruins, barrister's opening brief

indicators.note: ruins is a verb here: the letters that follow are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
a word's opening is its first letter, so take the start of barrister's

explanation.surface: A shaky witness wrecks the case the barrister opened with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' reads as a noun but is the anagram signal: B (the opening of barrister's) and BRIEF are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar is a person who tells fibs, the last thing a court wants from someone giving evidence.

clue.text: Nice chap, perhaps

parts.note: Nice, capitalised at the start, is the French Riviera city, so a man from there is a man of France rather than a pleasant fellow

explanation.walkthrough: The capital N is hidden by the clue's opening position: Nice is the city on the Côte d'Azur, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nice is one example of a male French citizen, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: With 20, one performing a great number

parts.note: the answer to 20 down is a man's name whose usual short form is Bill
one is the Roman numeral I
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: Together with a partner, somebody puts on a huge show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With 20' sends you to 20 down, the name WILLIAM, whose pet form BILL starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a huge count, the standard modern sense of the word.

clue.text: Exploring party dispatch

explanation.surface: An expedition force is sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A group on a journey of discovery is one sense; prompt speed, as in 'with all haste', is the other.

clue.text: One taking advantage of secret passage

definitions.text: One taking advantage of secret passage

parts.words: One taking advantage of secret passage
parts.note: passage reads as a hidden corridor but means a voyage, enjoyed in secret by someone hiding aboard without paying

explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' suggests a concealed tunnel in a house; it is a sea journey travelled illicitly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hides on a ship or plane to travel free gets a journey nobody knows about.

clue.text: Oft-repeated note about a private chat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the run of notes goes round the single letter
repeated doubles the run of notes again, so the note appears four times in all
oft, meaning often, says the note is written more than once

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A much-repeated memo concerns a confidential conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oft' and 'repeated' together give TE four times over; 'about' wraps those TETETETE letters round A, which lands in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for an intimate conversation between two people, literally head to head.

clue.text: Mark raised after 'strike, producing prosperity

explanation.surface: A welt from a blow somehow leads to good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge on the skin left by a lash is one sense; well-being, as in 'the common good', is the archaic other.

clue.text: How odd for wisest learner to be this!

definitions.text: How odd for wisest learner to be this!

indicators.note: an exclamation of oddness signals that the letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: L is the learner plate, the standard abbreviation for a learner driver

explanation.surface: It is strange that the cleverest student should turn out to be a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: WISEST plus L rearranged, and a sage pupil being foolish is indeed odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Being foolish or lacking sense is the very opposite of being the wisest.

clue.text: Bowls in place for white roses

explanation.surface: A bowler at a ground where white roses grow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who dismisses a batsman with a ball pitched at the feet is said to york him. The white rose is the emblem of Yorkshire, a county of northern England, abbreviated Yorks.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering a ball right at the batter's toes is one sense; the shortened county name with the rose emblem is the other.

clue.text: Furtively look up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same going up the grid as coming down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glancing secretly, eyes moving up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so it reads the same whichever direction you take in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a quick sly glance, as through a keyhole.

clue.text: Curved shape in otherwise round mouthpiece

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: otherwise means else, as in 'or else'
a lip is part of the mouth, a jocular mouth piece

explanation.surface: A curved shape on an otherwise round mouthpiece of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the shape but is the container signal; 'mouthpiece' suggests a brass instrument part, but here it is a piece of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval curve, a regular stretched circle in geometry.

clue.text: One vehicle or another turning to 'right

indicators.note: turning means the word for the second vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: another vehicle, following on from the first, is a cart

explanation.surface: A vehicle or a second one turning right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One vehicle or another' invites two definitions, but only the first defines; 'another' supplies the second vehicle, which 'turning' reverses to TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine for pulling ploughs is a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Precocious dramatic work easy to perform

explanation.surface: A gifted youngster's play is simple to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally, a play written by a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a drama by a youngster; idiomatically a task requiring no effort.

clue.text: Cross-benches addressed by minister

parts.note: cross-benches suggests the neutral seats in the House of Lords, but these are the benches of a church, marked by the cross, where the minister preaches to the congregation

explanation.walkthrough: Cross-benches in Parliament seat independent peers; minister suggests a government member, but here is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wooden seats in a church facing the pulpit where the preacher speaks.

clue.text: Appeal judge's work

parts.note: appeal judge suggests a senior court, but the appeal is a cricketer's shout for a dismissal, decided by the official on the field

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders appeal ('Howzat?') to the official who decides if the batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The role or office of the match official who rules on appeals in cricket.

clue.text: German city's Irish quarter

explanation.surface: A German city has an Irish district.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two senses. Ireland has four provinces, so one is a quarter of the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Westphalian city is one sense; one of Ireland's four historic provinces is the other.

clue.text: Encounter by chance what some answers do

explanation.surface: Meeting by accident, as answers do.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: entries in a crossword grid going left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone unexpectedly is one sense; across entries extend from left to right over the grid.

clue.text: 1 dn's in a group

parts.note: 1 down is a man from France, so the clue asks for his language's way of saying 'in a group'

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints '1 dn's', short for 1 down's; the answer there is a man from France, so this is his phrase for 'together'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English meaning all together, as a body.

clue.text: Keeping vital monarch in terrible revenge.

indicators.note: in places the monarch inside the rearranged letters
terrible says the letters of revenge are mangled into a new order

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A king clinging to life while plotting dreadful revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters to give EVGREEN, and 'in' slips the Queen's initials in after the first two letters. 'Keeping vital' means staying fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that stays green all year, keeping its leaves alive through winter, and so lasting freshness.

clue.text: Women replaced on our satellite at one stage.

indicators.note: replaced, read as re-placed, means the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Women have been put on the moon at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' reads as substituted but means re-placed, scrambling the women into NEWMO. 'our satellite at one stage' is a phase of the Moon, not the Moon itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phase when the Moon is dark at the start of its monthly cycle, one stage of it.

clue.text: Tell, for example, Carroll's old father

explanation.surface: The archer Tell, like the old man in Lewis Carroll.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero; Lewis Carroll's poem begins 'You are old, Father William'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss archer's first name is one sense; the aged parent in Carroll's verse in Alice is the other.

clue.text: Corresponding effort for record fibre production

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
istle is a tough plant fibre from Mexican agave, used for cord

explanation.surface: Joint work aimed at making records out of fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding' means writing letters, not matching. ISTLE is an obscure crossword fibre; 'for' and 'production' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter is the product of correspondence, a written effort sent to someone.

clue.text: Left publication for officer in Rome

explanation.surface: A left-wing paper for a Roman official.
explanation.walkthrough: Tribune is a long-running British left-wing weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist British magazine is one sense; a Roman magistrate protecting the plebeians is the other.

clue.text: Stop 'to think

explanation.surface: Pause for reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or wait, as in 'hold it', is one sense; to have an opinion, as in 'hold a view', is the other.

clue.text: Lead, possibly, from the centre

explanation.surface: Leadership possibly coming from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games you may lead a card from the suit marked with red symbols, so 'Lead, possibly' means a card played.
explanation.definitionFit: A card from one red suit is a possible opening play; the core or middle of something is the other sense.

clue.text: Broadcasting very little

explanation.surface: Sowing seed widely, though only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading seed widely by hand is one sense; a small sparse amount is the other.

clue.text: Fine part of something

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters inside the next word

explanation.surface: A good piece of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests good, but means slender or delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine thread is slender, the delicate sense of the word.

clue.text: Beautiful blonde

explanation.surface: A lovely fair-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely, as in 'fair lady', is one sense; light-coloured hair is the other.

clue.text: How to score in lively fashion

definitions.text: How to score in lively fashion

parts.words: How to score in lively fashion
parts.note: score suggests a game, but here a musical score carries an Italian direction telling players to perform with spirit

explanation.walkthrough: Composers write Italian performance directions in the score.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian tempo marking meaning animated, telling musicians to play briskly.

clue.text: Like MPs at work, perhaps, within organization

explanation.surface: Politicians busy in the Commons, inside the institution.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs work in the House of Commons, so they are literally in the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Members sitting in the chamber is the literal sense; done by staff rather than outsiders is the other.

clue.text: Shrub's flower is taken to king

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in England
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A shrub's bloom is presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom but means a river; the 's is a link and 'taken to' joins K on.
explanation.definitionFit: A feathery-leaved bush of salty coasts, a kind of shrub.

clue.text: Spotted outside piano, left inside organ

indicators.note: outside means the word for spotted goes around the musical letter

parts.note: spotted means seen
p is the musical marking for piano, soft
L is the standard abbreviation for left, which also sits inside the word for spotted

explanation.surface: A piano spotted outdoors, left inside a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps SEEN round P and L together; 'inside' simply restates that the L sits within as well, straight after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: An abdominal body part that filters blood is an organ.
